title: Juniper's Curly Decorations
markdown:
Oh, Juniper the deer loved sunny meadow days. She loved the tickle of sweet clover and the way dandelion wishes danced. Today was extra special — the Annual Sunny Meadow Picnic. Juniper’s biggest job was making the prettiest decorations ever. A flutter started in her chest. What if they aren’t perfect?

Her friend Rosie the lamb bounced up. “What shall we make, Juniper?”

Juniper’s nose twitched. “I have a splendid plan for the most perfect decorations.”

Ceridwen the squirrel scampered down. He was the champion of neatness. With his tidy paws, he laid out colourful paper, scissors, and string. “All ready,” he rustled.

Miss Clover, who minded the picnic cloths and never once scolded a dandelion for being crooked, set a basket of clips beside the string. “For when things want to curl,” she said, as if curls were invited.

Juniper looked at the neat supplies and Rosie’s happy bouncing. A tiny wobble of worry rippled through her again. What if my decorations aren’t perfect? What if Rosie makes a mess?

“First,” said Ceridwen, “we’ll cut pretty shapes.”

Juniper chose blue paper for a perfect butterfly. Rosie grabbed yellow paper and began to fold, giggling.

“Now, for the string,” Ceridwen continued. Juniper copied him precisely. Rosie, trying to tie her own knot, accidentally dropped her paper. Her hoof nudged a roll of sparkly red ribbon. Instead of a straight line, a short happy curl of ribbon sprang out and landed on her yellow paper.

“Oh, fiddlesticks,” sighed Rosie. “It’s all curly, not straight.”

Juniper saw Rosie’s paper. The cheerful yellow had a bright red curly ribbon. Juniper’s tummy did a nervous flip. “Oh, Rosie,” she whispered. “That curly ribbon… it looks… untidy.”

Ceridwen tilted his head. “Hmm,” he said thoughtfully. “That’s not untidy, Rosie. That’s… surprising. What if we put another curly bit right next to it?”

Juniper looked at Rosie. Rosie’s lip began to tremble. But then Rosie looked at Ceridwen’s twinkling eyes. Juniper thought about her neat plan. Then she looked at Rosie’s paper again. That curly ribbon looked like sunshine having a wonderful wiggly time. Maybe her plan could have fun and surprise too. Taking a deep breath, Juniper’s voice grew stronger. “Okay, Rosie,” she said with a smile. “Let’s try another curly bit.”

Rosie’s eyes lit up. She stuck another bright red curl next to the first. Juniper, feeling a new excitement bubble up, found a sparkly green ribbon and made a tiny joyful curl of her own. Ceridwen smiled and showed them how to tuck the ends so they’d stay put. Miss Clover clicked a clip onto the green curl, as if to say it belonged.

Soon their decorations were a delightful sight. Cheerful curly ribbons popped out everywhere, like happy surprises. The butterflies had curly wings that seemed to flutter. The sunny circles had curly sunbeams that looked ready to dance.

When it was time for the picnic, the meadow buzzed with happy chatter. Juniper and Rosie unfurled their wonderfully curly decorations. The other animals gasped. “Oh, how lovely,” exclaimed Mrs Hedgehog. “Those curly bits are so cheerful,” added Ferdinand the fox.

Juniper looked at the decorations, bursting with fun. She looked at Rosie, beaming. She looked at all the happy faces. Her worry had fluttered away. The picnic cloths, thanks to Miss Clover, stayed put. The ribbons, thanks to Rosie, did not.
characters: Juniper (a picnic-decorating deer), Rosie (a bouncing lamb), Miss Clover (a picnic-cloth minder)
author: StoryGen Community
